title: Long-command watchers
summary: A wrapper keeps every line in its raw capture and writes wake-worthy lines to its progress capture. yoke watch tail wakes its reader only on failures, refusals, decision-needing waits, terminal outcomes and the exit sentinel; routine digests and stall notices ride in front of the next such line, so a bare tail needs no filter. A fleet report reaches the reader as one write; a report that never closes, or that the watcher cut short with its report_partial note, is handed over at once and never holds a later fleet inbox or ALARM line. Watchers load runtime modules before starting the child, so terminal reporting and liveness retain the loaded code while the source changes; installed commands lease an immutable CLI release. A merge exit 9 is a designed wait only when its capture contains landing_pending with a backticked rerun command; the watcher uses that report and command as the cause and continuation. An unconfirmed queue entry remains a failure. Each fleet probe pass ends with a raw-only fleet pass line. An unchanged fleet stays silent in progress while passes complete; no child output within the existing quiet bound aborts with fleet_probe_stalled and waiting_on diagnosis, reaps the child group and wakes the reader to restart the watcher. The wrapper refuses fleet_probe_interval_invalid unless --interval is positive and below that bound.
